mem-001.summary: Concept aliases must be normalized during graph build, not just query time

mem-003.summary: graph_manager.add_memory() generates IDs by counting existing memory nodes — deleting any memory resets the counter and will silently overwrite the re-generated ID on the next insert [skills/nav-graph/functions/graph_manager.py:272]

mem-004.summary: correction_to_memory.py calls load_graph/save_graph inside the per-item loop, causing N file I/O cycles for N corrections; load once before the loop and save once after (see research_to_graph.py for the correct pattern) [skills/nav-graph/functions/correction_to_memory.py:88]

mem-005.summary: resolve_concept_alias() in graph_manager.py has no entries for 'performance', 'security', or 'configuration' — memories ingested by research_to_graph.py under those concepts are invisible to graph queries [skills/nav-graph/functions/graph_manager.py:169]

mem-006.summary: all three ingestion converters share the same sys.path.insert + from graph_manager import pattern for sibling-module resolution; new converters should follow this to stay consistent [skills/nav-graph/functions/research_to_graph.py:33]

mem-007.summary: research_to_graph.py sets DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE=0.7 (vs 0.8 for corrections, 0.95 for task decisions) — intentionally lower because agent inference is less authoritative than user-confirmed corrections [skills/nav-graph/functions/research_to_graph.py:37]

mem-008.summary: concept-extraction logic is duplicated in four places (correction_to_memory.py, task_to_graph.py, research_to_graph.py, graph_builder.py) with diverging keyword sets; research_to_graph.py's module-level KEYWORD_MAP is the most complete and the best candidate for extraction into a shared concept_extractor.py [skills/nav-graph/functions/research_to_graph.py:40]

mem-010.summary: All 4 fixes applied: mem-005 aliases, mem-003 ID gen, mem-004 batch I/O, mem-009 file creation [skills/nav-graph/functions/graph_manager.py:296]

mem-032.summary: Next.js 15+ fetch() is uncached by default — the opposite of v14. Pages re-render on every request unless you opt into caching with { next: { revalidate: N } } or { cache: 'force-cache' }. Most blog posts and muscle memory predate this flip. Lead templates with explicit { cache: 'no-store' } when SSR is the intent. See .agent/philosophy/NEXTJS-PATTERNS.md §D.

mem-033.summary: Next.js 16 renames middleware.ts to proxy.ts at project root. Same matcher API and NextRequest/NextResponse, but middleware.ts is deprecated. Codemod: npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy . Also in v15+: params and searchParams are Promises — must await them in pages, layouts, and route handlers. Route Handler context type is inferred from the file path: collection routes get Promise<{}>, dynamic routes get Promise<{id: string}>. Hardcoding the dynamic shape on a collection route fails  type-check. See .agent/philosophy/NEXTJS-PATTERNS.md §A, §E, §H.

mem-036.title: Plugin manifest hooks fail silently when $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DIR unset
mem-036.summary: v6.14.0 shell guard (if [ -n "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DIR" ]; then ... fi) exits 0 with no output when CC does not bind the variable — every hook becomes invisible no-op. Projects with project-local .claude/settings.json hardcoded entries mask the failure; manifest-only projects get zero injection and zero error signal. Fixed v6.15.1 via shell parameter-expansion fallback to flat marketplaces path.

mem-034.summary: Hook that exits 2 on UserPromptSubmit blocks the model entirely; stderr goes to the user not Claude. Compounding bug: if stderr echoes the original trigger phrase verbatim, the next prompt re-triggers the block recursively. Captured during v6.11.1 verification 2026-05-11.

mem-035.summary: Claude Code PreToolUse hook stdout AND hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext JSON produce zero visible output in model context. Only exit 2 (refuse tool) and accompanying stderr affect behavior. Captured during v6.12.0 live verification 2026-05-11.

mem-037.summary: Stop hook nav_workflow_state.py stamped check_shown=false on every assistant turn missing the literal WORKFLOW CHECK string, including AskUserQuestion-only and pure-text turns. workflow_enforcer.py then deadlocked the next loop-trigger prompt. Fixed in v6.15.3 by tristating check_shown — True if CHECK present, False only when prior turn used a codebase-mutating tool without showing it, None otherwise.
